newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Russian diplomat warns of potential nuclear threat.
newsitem.headline: Russian diplomat warns of potential nuclear threat.

text.p: A senior Russian diplomat said on Tuesday that enlarging NATO without Moscow's consent could create a nuclear threat against the United States and Europe.

Oleg Grinevsky, Russian ambassador to Sweden, said if the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) pushed ahead with its plans to expand without first reaching an agreement with Russia it would create nuclear tension in the region.
"Enlarging NATO will bring more reliance on the nuclear factor in Europe," Grinevsky told a U.S.-organised conference in Stockholm, titled The Baltic Region and The New European Security Structure.
"This is a real danger for the United States and Europe.
"To expand NATO in the manner in which it is doing now could bring a lot of trouble, and not only in the relations between Russia and Germany, Russia and the United States."

Grinevsky said Russia remained strongly opposed to NATO enlarging to the east, and was particularily against the movement of NATO military infrastructure -- and nuclear infrastructure -- to the borders of Russia.
Russia wants the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) Treaty recast to reflect the new Europe.

"It is necessary when talking about NATO enlargement to take into account Russian concerns," he said. "I think a compromise agreement is possible. It is really necessary to have some kind of agreement."
NATO is currently planning to take in a few former Eastern bloc nations as it prepares a new model of European security in the post-Cold War era.

No decision has yet been made on which countries will be admitted to the 16-member alliance in a first round of expansion but the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are tipped for early entry with Romania and Slovenia seen as possibles.
At the same time NATO is also trying to reach an agreement with Russia -- but says the two processes are not intertwined despite Russia's insistence that any treaty is signed first.
"We are afraid that NATO enlargement will destroy the present security structures and bases for these security structures existing in Europe," Grinevsky told the one-day conference.
"Now the military balance in Europe is three to one in favour of NATO. After NATO enlargement it will be four to one in favour of NATO."
Grinevsky said the reason for countries rushing to join NATO should not be hidden.
"It is not a secret that the main reason for these Eastern European or Baltic countries...to apply for NATO is that they are afraid of Russia," he said.
"We have the same fears with the NATO structure moving much closer to the Russian borders."
Grinevsky said Russia currently has sufficient nuclear forces to destroy the United States or Europe.
"If we are not enemies any more, to decrease this danger is very rational, but what is going on instead of this is discussions on enlarging NATO," Grinevsky said.
"The only answer from the military point of view is to rely on nuclear deterrence, to keep this."
But Grinevsky said Russia would not be the only party to resort to nuclear force.
"NATO will also rely more on nuclear because it needs to defend more territory with less conventional forces," he said.
